podcast.title: Formation and Continued Existence (1985-Present)
podcast.body: The band formed in 1985 and, despite a hiatus that began around 1996, continues to exist and perform occasional gigs. "They were formed in 1985, but there was a hiatus that started in about 1996, and today they get together to play a gig every once in a while."

podcast.title: FACTOR & VideoFACT Beneficiary
podcast.body: The band benefited from funding from both FACTOR and VideoFACT, which helped them make their record "I'm an Adult Now" and shoot a video for it, ultimately leading to a major label deal and a successful career. "Here's one band that benefited from both factor and video fact money."

podcast.title: Great Canadian Power Pop Band
podcast.body: The Pursuit of Happiness is recognized as "one of the great Canadian power pop bands of all time." "one of the great Canadian power pop bands of all time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Lost Canadian Bands 3

podcast.title: Late 1980s Success
podcast.body: Pursuit of Happiness was among the new acts signed throughout the late 1980s who achieved hits and solid-selling albums. This success was incentivized by the serious prospect of radio airplay, coverage by MuchMusic, and funding assistance, reflecting a growing investment in Canadian talent by the recorded music industry. "Throughout the late 1980s, new acts were signed and had hits in solid-selling albums, Blue Rodeo, The Box, Pursuit of Happiness, Northern Pikes, National Velvet, Alana Miles, 5440, Cowboy Junkeys."

podcast.title: Moe Berg in Supergroup The High Women
podcast.body: Moe Berg is a member of "The High Women," an on-again, off-again Canadian indie supergroup that also includes Chris Murphy of Sloan, Craig Northe of Odds, and Steven Page, formerly of Barenaked Ladies. "He's also part of an on-again, off-again Canadian indie supergroup called The High Women, with Chris Murphy of Sloan, Craig Northe of Odds, and Steve Page, ex of the Bearnick and Ladies."

xref.title: Rise in 1993
xref.body: Doo Boys began their rise in 1993, joining a wave of new Canadian artists gaining attention both domestically and internationally. This marked a period when foreign music fans started discovering Canadian talent.
